title: The Largest Sequence With Spaced Pairs

concept.title: Place the largest number first, and let the order of trying give the answer
body: Build a sequence of length `2n - 1` that contains the number `1` once and every number `i` from 2 to `n` twice, so that the two copies of `i` are exactly `i` positions apart (there are `i - 1` other numbers between them). Among all valid sequences we want the one that is **largest in dictionary order**: the first number as large as possible, then the second, and so on.

Fill the positions from left to right. At the first empty position try the numbers from the **largest to the smallest**: a number `i > 1` can go there only if the position `i` further on is empty too (both copies are placed at once), and the number 1 needs just this one position. Because the largest choice is tried first, the first complete sequence found is the largest one.

A valid sequence exists for every `n`, and the search finds the first one after a modest number of wrong tries. "Try the best choice first and stop at the first success" is the general way to get an extremal answer from backtracking, whenever the order of trying is the order of the answers.

statement: Given `n`, build a sequence of `2n - 1` integers in which the number 1 appears once and each of the numbers 2, 3, ..., `n` appears exactly twice, and the distance between the two copies of a number `i` (the difference of their positions) is exactly `i`. Print the sequence that is the largest in dictionary order (compare the first numbers, then the second numbers, and so on).

examples.note: The sequence 3 1 2 3 2 is valid: the 3s are 3 apart and the 2s are 2 apart. It is the largest one.

hints: Fill the first empty position; try the numbers from n down to 1.
A number i greater than 1 needs the position i further on to be empty; place both copies at once.
Return true as soon as the whole sequence is filled; undo the placement when a deeper call fails.

explanation: The first empty position is filled with the largest number that fits: a number `v > 1` needs the position `v` further on to be free, and then both copies are written. The first complete sequence found is the largest, because larger choices are tried first; failed placements are undone.
solution.complexity: Time: small for n <= 20 (the first success is found quickly), space O(n).
